0x61b2cf0.name: rocksdb::Tracer::MultiGet
quirks: The size check runs BEFORE the gate: when column_families.size() != keys.size() MultiGet returns Status::Corruption("the CFs size and keys size does not match!") at once -- the gate is never consulted, the clock is never read and the sampling counter is untouched, even when the MultiGet flag is set or the trace file is over the limit.

The size-mismatch message is the exact 42-byte string at .rodata 0x966820 ("the CFs size and keys size does not match!"), built by the Status(code, subcode, msg, msg2) constructor at 0x61cf670 with code 2 (kCorruption), subcode 0 and an empty second message (data 0x4376fd, size 0), so the state is the message alone.

The type byte lives in its own stack slot (rsp+0x5b) passed by address to ShouldSkipTrace, then copied into trace.type at rsp+0xc8 after the gate passes; ShouldSkipTrace reads the type through that pointer (movzbl 0x0(%rbp) at 0x61b1949).

The timestamp comes from the SystemClockWrapper::NowMicros fast path unrolled over 10 layers here (9 compared layers, the 10th called directly at 0x61b2eed without a comparison) -- IteratorSeekForPrev unrolls 12 layers; the depth is a code-generation artifact, and the observable result is the innermost clock's NowMicros() in both cases.

The loop bound and the encoded size are the LOW 32 bits of keys.size() (the loop bound is the zero-extended u32 at 0x61b2fc4; the encoded size is a 32-bit load at 0x61b3150) -- a keys.size() above 2^32 would loop over and encode the truncated count; untestable at that scale, recorded from the disassembly.

The varint length prefix encodes the LOW 32 bits of each key size (mov 0x8(%r14),%esi at 0x61b3062) and of each blob size (mov r12d,%esi at 0x61b31c3 and 0x61b3272) while the append copies the full size_t -- a >4 GiB key or blob would prefix the truncated length; untestable at that scale, recorded from the disassembly.

The payload_map is 0x700 unconditionally (bits 8, 9, 10) -- even for the empty multiget, where both blobs stay empty and the payload is just PutFixed64(0x700) + PutFixed32(0) + varint(0) + varint(0), 14 bytes.

Each CF id comes from a ColumnFamilyHandle vtable call (slot 3, +0x18, call at 0x61b3000) inside the per-key loop -- unlike IteratorSeek/SeekForPrev, where the caller already resolved the id; the binary does not null-check the handle pointer.

The exception landing pads at 0x61b3576..0x61b3595 (endbr64; mov r12,rax; jmp 0x61b2ca8 / 0x61b2cba) run only on the exception path (bad_alloc from the string appends); they jump to the shared cleanup fragment at 0x61b2ca8..0x61b2cd5, which disposes the three strings, checks the canary at rsp+0x108 and calls _Unwind_Resume. The string length guards raise length_error instead (std::string::_M_append, via __throw_length_error).

The three strings are freed only when their pointers differ from their SSO buffers (payload at rsp+0xd8/SSO rsp+0xe8, cfids at rsp+0x80/SSO rsp+0x90, keys at rsp+0xa0/SSO rsp+0xb0); the three 5-byte varint buffers sit at rsp+0xf9 (key), rsp+0xfe (cfids blob) and rsp+0x103 (keys blob), just below the stack canary at rsp+0x108.
rules: n_keys = (keys.end - keys.begin) >> 4 (16-byte Slices) and n_cf = (column_families.end - column_families.begin) >> 3 (8-byte pointers); when they differ, return Status::Corruption("the CFs size and keys size does not match!") at once (0x61b2d41..0x61b2db1), before the gate or the clock
if ShouldSkipTrace(this, type) (0x61b1930) returns true, return Status::OK() at once (no clock call, no writer call)
